documents.title: Artificial Intelligence at USD: Guidance and Principles
documents.summary: The hub gives USD's guidance and seven principles for responsible GenAI use. It says use varies by discipline and course, asks for disclosure, verification and data protection, and names Microsoft Copilot as the only fully approved tool. It states that it is guidance, not official policy.
documents.stance_why: The page says "The information provided here should not be viewed as official policy; it is intended to provide guidance" and "AI use will vary both between and within disciplines. Faculty should make this determination". It sets no ban or permission for coursework itself and leaves the decision to disciplines and courses, so delegates.

units.why: The opening sentence states the purpose of the hub: "to guide students, faculty, and staff in the ethical and innovative use of generative AI". It is an institution-level framework statement, so P56.
units.anchor: to guide students, faculty, and staff in the ethical and innovative use of generative AI

units.why: "should not be viewed as official policy; it is intended to provide guidance" sets the binding status of the whole page. No existing type covers the status of the document, so UNCOVERED rather than P56.
units.anchor: should not be viewed as official policy; it is intended to provide guidance
units.uncovered_note: The page states that its content is guidance, not official university policy.

units.why: "GenAI is an interactive set of tools that, when used, should serve as a supplement to human activity, not a replacement." This keeps humans as primary thinkers, so P32.
units.anchor: should serve as a supplement to human activity, not a replacement

units.why: "USD encourages transparency and accuracy ... with final work, decisions and strategies reflecting human judgment" asks for transparency about GenAI use; closest is P24 (disclosure), but the sentence is a general encouragement and also covers accuracy and human judgment.
units.anchor: USD encourages transparency and accuracy in the context of GenAI use
units.fit_note: Also asks for accuracy and for final work and decisions to reflect human judgment; no disclosure mechanism is given.

units.why: "All members of the USD community are expected to maintain professional and academic integrity when using these tools." A general expectation with no specific content, so P116.
units.anchor: expected to maintain professional and academic integrity when using these tools

units.why: "USD teaches and empowers our students, faculty and staff to understand and, when appropriate, to utilize with care the latest developments in technology, including GenAI" frames teaching AI literacy for the 21st century workplace, so P44.
units.anchor: USD teaches and empowers our students, faculty and staff to understand

units.why: "GenAI can help individuals brainstorm, iterate, and explore multiple angles" when users "question, verify and refine outputs". A permitted use for brainstorming with a condition, so P15.
units.anchor: GenAI can help individuals brainstorm, iterate, and explore multiple angles

units.why: "GenAI can help explore scientific questions, identify patterns, test hypotheses and make sense of non-sensitive data" names data analysis as a permitted use, so P89.
units.anchor: identify patterns, test hypotheses and make sense of non-sensitive data

units.why: "Effective GenAI requires that users develop clear goals, craft well-structured prompts, fact check output" gives practical prompting advice, so P93.
units.anchor: craft well-structured prompts, fact check output and reflect on their use of technology

units.why: "we recommend individuals use their critical thinking skills to assess, question and refine the GenAI answers" asks users to evaluate AI output, so P31.
units.anchor: we recommend individuals use their critical thinking skills to assess, question and refine

units.why: "employers expect graduates to understand where GenAI can effectively assist and where human expertise must lead" argues AI use is a professional skill, so P44.
units.anchor: employers expect graduates to understand where GenAI can effectively assist

units.why: "We encourage faculty, staff and students to use this tool" (Microsoft 365 Copilot, the "approved GenAI chat") points to the institution-approved tool, so P92 not P17 (institution-wide, not one course).
units.anchor: We encourage faculty, staff and students to use this tool

units.why: "Individuals can view a list of AI tools approved for various uses and their security level in Coyote One Stop." Directs readers to the approved list, so P92.
units.anchor: list of AI tools approved for various uses and their security level

units.why: "GenAI is a resource available to the university’s community, not a requirement for every academic or professional pursuit." AI is optional, which sits nearest P51 (not required), though the stated aim is not equity.
units.anchor: not a requirement for every academic or professional pursuit
units.fit_note: Says AI is not required for every pursuit; it does not mention cost or access.

units.why: "Its role will vary across disciplines, courses, assignments and/or projects." The rule is left to disciplines and courses, so P04.
units.anchor: Its role will vary across disciplines, courses, assignments and/or projects.

units.why: "USD’s priority is maintaining the integrity of learning and inquiry while upholding the academic standards and expectations of individual courses". A stated reason grounded in integrity of learning, so P95 rather than P41 because it is not about skill-building.
units.anchor: maintaining the integrity of learning and inquiry

units.why: "Ethical and professional use of GenAI requires examining, verifying and reflecting on outputs" and treating GenAI "as a drafting or exploratory partner, rather than an authority". Verification duty, so P31.
units.anchor: requires examining, verifying and reflecting on outputs

units.why: "USD will review this guidance regularly and update it to reflect evolving technologies, BOR policy, scholarship, legal frameworks and stakeholder input." A review cycle, so P54.
units.anchor: USD will review this guidance regularly and update it

units.why: Principle 1 says "Independent thinking and deep learning emerge from the responsible and ethical use of information and technology". A learning-first principle without a specific rule, closest P32.
units.anchor: Independent thinking and deep learning emerge from the responsible and ethical use
units.fit_note: A principle that learning depends on independent thinking; it does not tell students to remain the primary problem-solver.

units.why: Principle 2: "AI use will vary both between and within disciplines." AI rules differ by discipline and within, so P04.
units.anchor: AI use will vary both between and within disciplines.

units.why: "Faculty should make this determination in collaboration with peers and academic leadership, guided by disciplinary norms, accreditation requirements and course outcomes." Asks instructors to align decisions with colleagues and discipline, so P109.
units.anchor: Faculty should make this determination in collaboration with peers and academic leadership
units.fit_note: Also ties the decision to accreditation requirements and course outcomes.

units.why: Principle 3: "students, faculty and staff should disclose how it was used and cite sources or models where relevant". Disclosure when AI contributes meaningfully, so P24.
units.anchor: should disclose how it was used and cite sources or models where relevant
units.fit_note: Disclosure is conditioned on AI meaningfully contributing and on instructor or program guidance.

units.why: "Users must validate claims with credible sources, note limitations" under the heading that "AI can be incorrect or biased." Verification duty, so P31.
units.anchor: Users must validate claims with credible sources, note limitations

units.why: "avoid overreliance on AI for facts, analysis or authorship" warns against AI replacing the user's own thinking and authorship, so P32.
units.anchor: avoid overreliance on AI for facts, analysis or authorship

units.why: "Do not enter confidential, personally identifiable or proprietary information into AI tools without explicit authorization". A data-protection ban with an authorization exception, so P50.
units.anchor: Do not enter confidential, personally identifiable or proprietary information into AI tools

units.why: "Respect creators’ rights and licensing." Concerns the rights of creators in AI inputs and outputs, so P52.
units.anchor: Respect creators’ rights and licensing.

units.why: "If used, AI should be deployed in ways that broaden access to all learning materials and support all learners." Accessibility principle, so P97.
units.anchor: AI should be deployed in ways that broaden access to all learning materials

units.why: "AI outputs should not be considered a definitive conclusion" tells users to treat output as provisional, so P31.
units.anchor: AI outputs should not be considered a definitive conclusion.

units.why: Users "remain accountable for final decisions" makes the human responsible for what they act on, so P29 (own what you submit and decide).
units.anchor: remain accountable for final decisions
units.fit_note: Applies to decisions generally, not specifically to submitted coursework.

units.why: "The first draft of this page was written with the assistance of GenAI ... reviewed and refined by USD faculty and staff over the course of several months". Describes how the guidance was made, so P84.
units.anchor: reviewed and refined by USD faculty and staff over the course of several months

units.why: "GenAI refers to tools that can generate content—such as text, images, code, audio or video—based on prompts or questions." A definition that sets scope, so P61.
units.anchor: refers to tools that can generate content

units.why: "we encourage students to explore AI as a learning partner, not a replacement for their own thinking." Encourages AI use for learning while keeping the student thinking, so P02 with a note.
units.anchor: we encourage students to explore AI as a
units.fit_note: The encouragement is limited by the rule that AI must not replace the student's own thinking.

units.why: "GenAI tools must be reviewed and approved before use on campus." Institutional review before deployment, so P65.
units.anchor: GenAI tools must be reviewed and approved before use on campus.

units.why: "USD’s Information Technology Department provides information on which tools have passed review and what kinds of data or information are acceptable within each platform." Names IT as the office that publishes approved status, so P80.
units.anchor: Information Technology Department provides information on which tools have passed review

units.why: "Microsoft Copilot is the only tool on USD’s campus that is approved for full, integrated use." Institution-wide approved-tool rule, so P92.
units.anchor: Copilot is the only tool on USD’s campus that is approved for full, integrated use.

units.why: "Please note, use of AI may not be allowed in certain courses or appropriate in all contexts." Leaves permission to courses, so P04.
units.anchor: use of AI may not be allowed in certain courses or appropriate in all contexts

units.why: "AI should be used as a tool, not a replacement for human communication" and AI text "should not be sent as-is". Community members' own messages, closest P58 (students write their own course communication) but broader.
units.anchor: AI should be used as a tool, not a replacement for human communication
units.fit_note: Applies to all community communication, not only student messages to course staff.

units.why: "GenAI can help you start a draft or organize ideas" permits AI help with drafting and organizing text, so P91.
units.anchor: GenAI can help you start a draft or organize ideas

documents.unit: University of South Dakota (AI hub, Faculty)
documents.title: Generative AI Information: Faculty
documents.summary: Guidance for faculty on setting and communicating AI expectations, using AI in teaching and research, protecting data, and responding to suspected misuse through conversation and process. It recommends against relying on detection tools.
documents.stance_why: The page tells faculty to state "whether AI use is allowed, limited or prohibited in each course syllabus" and sets no rule of its own about whether students may use AI, so decisions are delegated to instructors.

units.why: "GenAI is understood as a tool ... best positioned as supplements to human expertise and judgment, not replacements for faculty knowledge, disciplinary standards or pedagogical intent." Keeps human expertise primary, so P32.
units.anchor: supplements to human expertise and judgment, not replacements for faculty knowledge

units.why: "GenAI is part of the professional landscape our graduates will encounter." Career-based reason for engaging students with AI, so P44.
units.anchor: GenAI is part of the professional landscape our graduates will encounter.

units.why: "please reach out to the Center for Teaching and Learning" points faculty to support for using GenAI in courses, so P63.
units.anchor: please reach out to the Center for Teaching and Learning

units.why: "GenAI refers to tools that can create new content such as text, images, code, audio or video" defines the scope, so P61.
units.anchor: refers to tools that can create new content such as text, images, code

units.why: "Faculty are responsible for clearly communicating expectations regarding AI use in their courses." Instructors must state AI expectations, so P09.
units.anchor: Faculty are responsible for clearly communicating expectations regarding AI use

units.why: "If no guidance is provided, students may make incorrect assumptions about acceptable use." Gives the reason for stating expectations; it does not set a fallback rule, so P09 as rationale.
units.anchor: If no guidance is provided, students may make incorrect assumptions about acceptable use.
units.fit_note: Rationale for stating expectations; no default rule when the syllabus is silent (so not P06).

units.why: "Stating whether AI use is allowed, limited or prohibited in each course syllabus." Syllabus statement, so P09.
units.anchor: Stating whether AI use is allowed, limited or prohibited in each course syllabus.
units.policy: Setting expectations may include stating whether AI use is allowed, limited or prohibited in each course syllabus.

units.why: "Identifying which tools are permitted." An instructor communicates which AI tools students may use; closest P09.
units.anchor: Identifying which tools are permitted.
units.policy: Setting expectations may include identifying which AI tools are permitted.
units.fit_note: Specifically about naming permitted tools.

units.why: "Explaining disclosure or citation requirements." Instructors communicate disclosure rules; closest P09 since it is about communicating, not setting, the rule.
units.anchor: Explaining disclosure or citation requirements.
units.policy: Setting expectations may include explaining disclosure or citation requirements.
units.fit_note: Specifically about explaining disclosure or citation requirements to students.

units.why: "Providing students with reasoning for why AI will or will not be used for various activities" asks instructors to explain their rules, so P66.
units.anchor: Providing students with reasoning for why AI will or will not be used

units.why: "Reinforcing expectations throughout the semester to ensure students remain cognizant." Repeated discussion of the rules beyond the syllabus, so P66.
units.anchor: Reinforcing expectations throughout the semester

units.why: "Modelling responsible AI use with students when use is appropriate for the course context." Instructors model use, so P112.
units.anchor: Modelling responsible AI use with students

units.why: "Overreliance on AI can: Weaken student skill development; Obscure authentic learning evidence; Create academic integrity concerns." Limits AI because it undermines practice, so P41.
units.anchor: Weaken student skill development

units.why: "Faculty are encouraged to design assignments that emphasize process, reflection, iteration and critical engagement rather than polished final products alone." Assignment redesign, so P35.
units.anchor: design assignments that emphasize process, reflection, iteration and critical engagement

units.why: "When faculty use AI in teaching materials, research or professional work: Be transparent where appropriate." Faculty disclosure of their own AI use, so P47.
units.anchor: Be transparent where appropriate
units.fit_note: Transparency is not tied to students and is limited to where appropriate; covers research and professional work too.

units.why: "Follow disciplinary and publisher citation norms" when faculty use AI in teaching materials, research or professional work. A citation rule for faculty, so P24.
units.anchor: Follow disciplinary and publisher citation norms
units.fit_note: Applies to faculty use, deferring to disciplinary and publisher norms.

units.why: "Model ethical disclosure practices for students" makes faculty disclosure an example for students, so P112.
units.anchor: Model ethical disclosure practices for students

units.why: "Faculty should not enter sensitive or restricted data into unapproved AI tools, including: Student records or student work". Data protection, so P50.
units.anchor: Faculty should not enter sensitive or restricted data into unapproved AI tools

units.why: "USD’s preferred and approved platform for GenAI is Microsoft Copilot, while using a USD work or school account". Points to the university-approved tool, so P92.
units.anchor: preferred and approved platform for GenAI is Microsoft Copilot

units.why: "Faculty should expect and plan for AI errors" and treat output as "suggestions, not authoritative answers". Verify output, so P31.
units.anchor: Faculty should expect and plan for AI errors.

units.why: "Consider disclosing GenAI use to students to model transparency in the teaching and learning process." Instructor discloses own AI use, so P47.
units.anchor: Consider disclosing GenAI use to students to model transparency

units.why: "Review assessment instructions for clarity" is a listed way faculty may use AI in course design, so P59.
units.anchor: Review assessment instructions for clarity.
units.policy: Faculty may use AI to review assessment instructions for clarity.

units.why: "Generate sample prompts, discussion starters or practice questions." Instructor use of AI for course materials, so P59.
units.anchor: Generate sample prompts, discussion starters or practice questions.
units.policy: Faculty may use AI to generate sample prompts, discussion starters or practice questions.

units.why: "Create examples that students can critique or revise." Instructor use of AI for teaching examples, so P59.
units.anchor: Create examples that students can critique or revise.
units.policy: Faculty may use AI to create examples that students can critique or revise.

units.why: "Explore multiple explanations of complex concepts." Instructor use of AI for teaching, so P59.
units.anchor: Explore multiple explanations of complex concepts.
units.policy: Faculty may use AI to explore multiple explanations of complex concepts.

units.why: "Support accessibility goals through generating alt text, creating alternative formats or drafting summaries." AI as an accessibility aid, so P97 over P59.
units.anchor: generating alt text, creating alternative formats or drafting summaries

units.why: "GenAI should not replace faculty judgment, grading or evaluative decision-making." Humans decide grades, so P46.
units.anchor: GenAI should not replace faculty judgment, grading or

units.why: "Student work and student data should not be entered into GenAI tools that are not approved for integrated use by the USD IT Department." Data protection for student work, so P50.
units.anchor: Student work and student data should not be entered into GenAI tools

units.why: "Reviewing faculty-drafted feedback language to help clarify action items" is an AI-assisted feedback use under the heading "(With Caution)" with human drafting first, so P101.
units.anchor: Reviewing faculty-drafted feedback language to help clarify action items

units.why: "Identifying patterns in student responses so that more specific and substantive feedback can be provided." AI-assisted feedback, so P101.
units.anchor: Identifying patterns in student responses

units.why: "Generating rubrics or criteria drafts to help students better understand how work will be assessed." Instructor use of AI for teaching materials, so P59.
units.anchor: Generating rubrics or criteria drafts

units.why: "Depending on disciplinary norms and publication expectations, AI may be used to enhance the research process." Research use, so P62.
units.anchor: AI may be used to enhance the research process

units.why: "Support literature exploration or summary" is a permitted research use of AI, so P104.
units.anchor: Support literature exploration or summary

units.why: "Assist with code, data cleaning or documentation" is a permitted research use, so P62 (research and scholarship).
units.anchor: Assist with code, data cleaning or documentation
units.fit_note: Names code and data cleaning as permitted research uses.

units.why: "Draft outlines or rephrase text for clarity" is a permitted research writing use, so P91.
units.anchor: Draft outlines or rephrase text for clarity

units.why: "USD faculty should ensure all scholarly contributions remain grounded in their own expertise and analysis." Research and scholarship rule, so P62.
units.anchor: scholarly contributions remain grounded in their own expertise and analysis

units.why: "Apply rigorous validation to AI-generated content and adhere to ethical standards, disciplinary norms, intellectual property expectations and any sponsor, regulatory or data use requirements." Research rule deferring to sponsors and norms, so P62.
units.anchor: adhere to ethical standards, disciplinary norms, intellectual property expectations

units.why: "Protect sensitive, confidential or proprietary research data by using only approved tools and workflows." Data protection, so P50.
units.anchor: using only approved tools and workflows

units.why: "Document GenAI use to maintain transparency and integrity in the research record." Research documentation, so P62.
units.anchor: Document GenAI use to maintain transparency and integrity in the research record.

units.why: "Misrepresenting GenAI-generated work as human-generated by students or faculty may raise academic misconduct under USD policy". Classifies misrepresentation as misconduct, so P36.
units.anchor: may raise academic misconduct under USD policy or professional ethics concerns

units.why: "Faculty are encouraged to address GenAI explicitly as part of academic integrity conversations". Discussing the rules with students, so P66.
units.anchor: address GenAI explicitly as part of academic integrity conversations

units.why: "detection tools, which are unreliable and raise privacy concerns" are not to be relied on, so P39.
units.anchor: rather than relying solely on detection tools, which are unreliable and raise privacy concerns

units.why: Tools that give "scores" such as Turnitin and Respondus Monitor "should be verified and human reviewed before decisions about academic misconduct are made". Output only supporting evidence, so P69.
units.anchor: should be verified and human reviewed before decisions about academic misconduct are made

units.why: "No single indicator proves AI use." A standard of evidence, so P69.
units.anchor: No single indicator proves AI use.

units.why: "multiple patterns together may warrant a conversation with the student" says to talk with the student before escalating, so P57.
units.anchor: multiple patterns together may warrant a conversation with the student

units.why: "Fluent writing with limited depth, original insight or disciplinary specificity" lists a sign of AI content, which is evidence the instructor may weigh, so P69.
units.anchor: Fluent writing with limited depth, original insight or disciplinary specificity.
units.fit_note: Lists a sign to weigh (overly polished but shallow responses), not a standard of proof.

units.why: "Formatting commonly found in GenAI output" lists structural signs of AI content, so P69.
units.anchor: Formatting commonly found in GenAI output
units.fit_note: Lists a sign to weigh (generic structure and language), not a standard of proof.

units.why: "Missing, incorrect or fabricated citations" is listed as a sign of AI content, so P69.
units.anchor: Missing, incorrect or fabricated citations.
units.fit_note: Lists a sign to weigh (lack of engagement with course materials), not a standard of proof.

units.why: "Errors that reflect common AI misunderstandings rather than novice human reasoning" is listed as a sign of AI content, so P69.
units.anchor: Errors that reflect common AI misunderstandings rather than novice human reasoning.
units.fit_note: Lists a sign to weigh (confident inaccuracies), not a standard of proof.

units.why: "the recommended next step is engagement and education, not accusation." Educative response to suspected misuse, so P68.
units.anchor: the recommended next step is engagement and education, not accusation

units.why: "Asking students to explain or defend their work orally." Checks understanding by explanation, so P34.
units.anchor: Asking students to explain or defend their work orally.
units.policy: When GenAI use is suspected, instructors may ask students to explain or defend their work orally.

units.why: "Requesting drafts, annotations, or reflections on decision-making" asks students for process evidence and reflections, so P26.
units.anchor: Requesting drafts, annotations, or reflections on decision-making.
units.policy: When GenAI use is suspected, instructors may request drafts, annotations or reflections on decision-making.
units.fit_note: Used by the instructor as a response to suspicion, not as a standing student duty.

units.why: "Having students identify challenges they faced and how they addressed them." A reflection used to check understanding, so P34.
units.anchor: Having students identify challenges they faced and how they addressed them.
units.policy: When GenAI use is suspected, instructors may have students identify challenges they faced and how they addressed them.

units.why: "Faculty are encouraged to frame concerns around learning outcomes, not tool use." Educative handling of concerns, so P68 with a note.
units.anchor: frame concerns around learning outcomes, not tool use
units.fit_note: Concerns are framed by learning outcomes rather than by whether a tool was used; no mention of first offenses or good faith.

units.why: "Can the student explain their reasoning and choices?" is a question for checking understanding of submitted work, so P34.
units.anchor: Can the student explain their reasoning and choices?

units.why: "Assignments that emphasize process, iteration and reflection naturally reduce misuse and make student thinking more visible." Assignment redesign, so P35.
units.anchor: emphasize process, iteration and reflection naturally reduce misuse

units.why: "Faculty should try to remain aware of these features and help students understand when AI is involved." Covers AI built into word processors and LMS, so P07.
units.anchor: help students understand when AI is involved
units.fit_note: Asks for awareness and explanation to students; it does not require disabling features.

units.why: "Automatically rewrites, summarizes or expands content" is a sign that a tool is using AI, a definition of scope for embedded AI, so P61.
units.anchor: Automatically rewrites, summarizes or expands content
units.fit_note: Defines when an embedded tool counts as AI.

documents.unit: University of South Dakota (AI hub, Students)
documents.title: Generative AI Information: Students
documents.summary: Guidance for students: AI may support learning in many ways but must not write papers or replace reading, must be cited per course rules, and must be used with attention to data protection. It tells students to follow each instructor's policy.
documents.stance_why: The page says "Follow Your Instructor’s Policies. Every class may have different rules" and "Some instructors allow AI freely; some allow it with limitations and others prohibit it for certain assignments". The core expectations do not set a single permission or ban, so delegates.

units.why: "Expand on ideas for projects or papers" is listed as a way GenAI "might be used to enhance learning" "when appropriate for context and discipline", so P15.
units.anchor: Expand on ideas for projects or papers
units.policy: When appropriate for context and discipline, GenAI might be used to expand on ideas for projects or papers.

units.why: "Support finding or searching for resources, information, research etc." is a listed use, so P104.
units.anchor: Support finding or searching
units.policy: When appropriate for context and discipline, GenAI might be used to support finding or searching for resources, information, research etc.

units.why: "Summarize complex readings or explain difficult concepts" is a listed use, so P12 (tutor for concepts). It conflicts with a later line that AI should not "Replace reading course materials".
units.anchor: Summarize complex readings
units.policy: When appropriate for context and discipline, GenAI might be used to summarize complex readings or explain difficult concepts.
units.fit_note: Also permits summarizing readings, which a later line limits.

units.why: "Generate practice questions to study for exams" is a listed use, so P14.
units.anchor: Generate practice questions to study for exams
units.policy: When appropriate for context and discipline, GenAI might be used to generate practice questions to study for exams.

units.why: "Help organize notes to improve understanding of concepts" is a listed study use, so P14.
units.anchor: Help organize notes
units.policy: When appropriate for context and discipline, GenAI might be used to help organize notes to improve understanding of concepts.

units.why: "Outline essays or presentations" is a listed writing support use, so P91.
units.anchor: Outline essays or presentations
units.policy: When appropriate for context and discipline, GenAI might be used to outline essays or presentations.

units.why: "Explore examples, such as sample code or problem-solving steps" is a listed use that explores approaches, so P15.
units.anchor: Explore examples,
units.policy: When appropriate for context and discipline, GenAI might be used to explore examples, such as sample code or problem-solving steps.
units.fit_note: Names sample code explicitly.

units.why: "Improve clarity in writing or refine drafts" is a listed writing support use, so P91.
units.anchor: Improve clarity
units.policy: When appropriate for context and discipline, GenAI might be used to improve clarity in writing or refine drafts.

units.why: "AI is a powerful tool—but it works best when you stay actively engaged, evaluate the output critically and make it your own." Keeps the student engaged and the owner of the work, so P32.
units.anchor: stay actively engaged, evaluate the output critically and make it your own
units.fit_note: Also asks students to evaluate output and make it their own.

units.why: "While instructors may set more specific rules for their courses, here are core expectations" leaves course-level detail to instructors, so P04.
units.anchor: instructors may set more specific rules for their courses

units.why: "Always check the syllabus, assignment instructions or ask your instructor for AI guidelines." Students find out the rule that applies, so P78.
units.anchor: Always check the syllabus, assignment instructions

units.why: "or ask your instructor for AI guidelines" tells students to ask the instructor, so P10.
units.anchor: or ask your instructor for AI guidelines

units.why: "Every class may have different rules; this is expected as it models real-life use of GenAI." Each class sets its own rules, so P11 (and the rationale is modelling real use).
units.anchor: Every class may have different rules
units.fit_note: Also gives the reason that varied rules model real-life AI use.

units.why: "Some instructors allow AI freely; some allow it with limitations and others prohibit it for certain assignments." Describes three categories of instructor rules, so P05 with a note since they are not named tiers.
units.anchor: Some instructors allow AI freely; some allow it with limitations
units.fit_note: Describes kinds of instructor rules but defines no named tiers.

units.why: "AI should not: Write your papers for you" bans AI-written submissions, so P19.
units.anchor: Write your papers for you

units.why: "Complete graded assignments that reflect your own understanding" bans AI doing graded work, so P19.
units.anchor: Complete graded assignments that reflect your own understanding

units.why: "Replace reading course materials" bans AI substituting for reading, so P105 (AI for reading and summarizing sources).
units.anchor: Replace reading course materials
units.fit_note: Bans replacing reading, while another line lists summarizing readings as a possible use.

units.why: "Overreliance on AI can harm your learning and violate academic integrity policies." Gives the learning reason, so P41.
units.anchor: Overreliance on AI can harm your learning

units.why: "If you use AI to support your work, follow your course or program’s citation guidelines." Students cite AI per course rules, so P24.
units.anchor: follow your course or program’s citation guidelines

units.why: "Common citation formats (APA, MLA, Chicago) now include ways to cite GenAI output." Points to citation guidance, so P115.
units.anchor: now include ways to cite GenAI output

units.why: "when you use unprotected GenAI tools, the inputs or data you share might be used to train models" warns about data use by tools, so P50.
units.anchor: the inputs or data you share might be used to train models

units.why: "Ensure you are using a protected platform when entering sensitive information" (own, other students', instructor, research or confidential data). Data protection, so P50.
units.anchor: Ensure you are using a protected platform when entering sensitive information

units.why: "USD’s preferred and protected tool is Microsoft Copilot, though other tools are approved for limited use." Points to the approved tool, so P92.
units.anchor: preferred and protected tool is Microsoft Copilot

units.why: "AI can sometimes: Create incorrect or misleading information; Fabricate citations; Present biased or incomplete answers." Output can be wrong, so P31.
units.anchor: Create incorrect or misleading information

units.why: "Always check accuracy against trusted sources." Students verify output, so P31.
units.anchor: Always check accuracy against trusted sources.

units.why: "Using GenAI in ways that misrepresent your own work may be considered academic misconduct under USD policy." Classes misrepresentation as misconduct, so P36.
units.anchor: misrepresent your own work may be considered academic misconduct under USD policy

units.why: "If you’re unsure whether something is acceptable, ask your instructor or consult the USD Student Rights and Responsibilities site." Ask when unsure, so P10.
units.anchor: If you’re unsure whether something is acceptable, ask your instructor

units.why: "Start with your own ideas before turning to AI." A sequencing rule, so P90.
units.anchor: Start with your own ideas

units.why: "Ask specific questions rather than vague ones." Prompting advice, so P93.
units.anchor: Ask specific questions

units.why: "Try multiple prompts to compare outputs." Prompting advice, so P93.
units.anchor: Try multiple prompts

units.why: "Edit and personalize and AI generated text." Asks students to make AI text their own, so P29 with a note.
units.anchor: Edit and personalize
units.fit_note: Frames ownership as editing and personalizing AI text; it does not forbid submitting AI text.

units.why: "Document what you used AI for (e.g., brainstorming, proofreading)." Students note their AI use, so P24.
units.anchor: Document what you used AI for
units.fit_note: Tip-level advice to note what AI was used for; no submission requirement.

units.why: "Students should not assume that a tool does not use AI simply because it is familiar." Covers embedded AI features, so P07.
units.anchor: Students should not assume that a tool does not use AI
units.fit_note: Asks students to recognize embedded AI; does not say to disable it.

units.why: "Automatically rewrites, summarizes, paraphrases or expands text" is a sign a tool uses AI, defining embedded AI, so P61.
units.anchor: Automatically rewrites, summarizes, paraphrases or expands text.
units.fit_note: Defines when an embedded tool counts as AI.

notes: Coded as Coder B. The hub says its content is guidance, not official policy. The student page lists summarizing readings as a possible use but also says AI should not replace reading course materials. Course syllabi were deferred in the collect file.
